# fastsae: High-Performance Frequentist and Bayesian Small Area Estimation in R

**fastsae** implements widely used Small Area Estimation (SAE) models
for survey data. Frequentist estimation runs in compiled **C++**
(`RcppArmadillo`) with **OpenMP** multi-threading, and Bayesian
estimation uses **INLA** (Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations).
With hundreds to thousands of domains it is much faster than existing R
implementations (see [Performance at a
Glance](#performance-at-a-glance); with a few dozen domains `sae` is
about as fast), while agreeing numerically with reference packages such
as `sae`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why fastsae?

- ⚡ **Speed**: with 1,000 domains, the C++ Fisher-scoring fits with
  analytical MSE are 29 to 1,250 times faster than `sae`
  (spatio-temporal model: 40 s instead of 19 minutes); with a few dozen
  domains the differences are a fraction of a second.
- 🎯 **Numerical agreement**: on the same data, coefficients, variance
  components, EBLUPs and analytical MSEs match `sae` (Molina &
  Marhuenda) to about $`10^{-14}`$; the documented exceptions are a
  spatial correlation on the boundary and the ML MSE of the spatial
  model.
- 🔀 **Frequentist and Bayesian in one package**: EBLUP models in C++
  and hierarchical Bayesian models through INLA.
- 🧵 **Parallel bootstrap**: multi-core OpenMP parametric and
  non-parametric bootstrap MSE estimation.
- 🗺️ **Unsampled areas**: domains with missing observations (`y = NA`)
  are predicted automatically.
- 💾 **Low memory**: avoids unnecessary $`O(m^2)`$ / $`O(m^3)`$
  allocations.
- 📊 **Standard R interface**: S3 methods (`summary`, `coef`, `fitted`,
  `residuals`) and publication-ready
  [`autoplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Understanding INLA: Fast Bayesian Inference without MCMC

**INLA** (Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations; Rue et al., 2009)
provides a deterministic alternative to Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
for Bayesian inference in latent Gaussian models. Instead of drawing
thousands of samples, INLA:

- **Approximates** posterior marginals analytically using Laplace
  approximations
- **Integrates** out non-Gaussian observations analytically
- **Delivers** results in seconds rather than hours

`fastsae` uses INLA through the
[`INLA`](https://www.r-inla-download.org) R package to fit hierarchical
Bayesian small area models with:

- **6 likelihood families**: Gaussian, Beta, Binomial, Poisson, Negative
  Binomial, Gamma
- **Spatial random effects**: Besag ICAR, BYM, BYM2, Leroux, SAR,
  spatial lag
- **Temporal random effects**: RW1, RW2, AR(1)
- **Spatio-temporal interactions**: separable and non-separable
  structures

**Compared with MCMC**: no chains to run and monitor, deterministic
results, and fits in seconds. INLA is an approximation: fastsae chose
its settings by comparing them with exact posteriors and long Stan runs,
and `engine = jax_engine()` fits the same models by MCMC when a check is
needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two-Fold Subarea Models: Nested Hierarchical Structure

The two-fold subarea model (Torabi & Rao, 2014) extends the standard
Fay-Herriot model to hierarchical data where **subareas are nested
within areas**:

``` math
y_{ij} = x_{ij}^\top \beta + v_i + u_{ij} + e_{ij}
```

where: - $`v_i \sim N(0, \sigma_v^2)`$: **Area-level random effect** -
$`u_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma_u^2)`$: **Subarea-level random effect** -
$`e_{ij} \sim N(0, D_{ij})`$: Sampling error with known variance

**Available implementations:** -
[`eblup_twofold()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_twofold.md):
Frequentist EBLUP via REML Fisher-scoring (C++) -
[`hb_twofold()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_twofold.md):
Bayesian hierarchical model via INLA with spatial support

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Comparison with Other Packages

| Feature | `fastsae` | `sae` (Molina & Rao) | `emdi` (Kreutzmann et al.) |
|:---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **Core Computation** | **C++ (RcppArmadillo)** | Pure R | R / lme4 / nlme |
| **Multi-Threading** | **Native OpenMP** (`n_threads`) | Single-threaded | Optional foreach/parallel |
| **Agreement with `sae` on the same data** | **About $`10^{-14}`$** | Reference | About $`10^{-6}`$ (convergence tolerance) |
| **Unsampled Area Support** | **Automatic (synthetic, kriging for spatial models)** | Manual subsetting required | Synthetic (out-of-sample domains) |
| **Bootstrap MSE** | **Parallel C++ (OpenMP)** | R | R |
| **S3 Methods Support** | `print`, `summary`, `coef`, `fitted`, `residuals`, `autoplot` | Custom lists | Standard S3 |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Supported Models

### Frequentist Models (EBLUP, C++)

| Model | Function | Random Effect Structure | MSE Estimation |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Fay-Herriot** (Area-level) | [`eblup_fh()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_fh.md) | Independent area effects | Analytical (Prasad-Rao) |
| **Spatial Fay-Herriot** | [`eblup_sfh()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_sfh.md) | SAR(1) spatial autocorrelation | Analytical, Bootstrap |
| **Spatio-Temporal Fay-Herriot** | [`eblup_stfh()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_stfh.md) | SAR(1) + Temporal AR(1) | Analytical, Bootstrap |
| **Battese-Harter-Fuller** (Unit-level) | [`eblup_bhf()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_bhf.md) | Random intercept nested in domains | Bootstrap |
| **Two-Fold Subarea** | [`eblup_twofold()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_twofold.md) | Area + Subarea nested effects | Analytical, Bootstrap |

### Bayesian Models (INLA)

| Model | Function | Distributions | Spatial/Temporal |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Area-level HB** | [`hb_area()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_area.md) | Gaussian, Beta, Binomial, Poisson, NB, Gamma | ✓ Full support |
| **Unit-level HB** | [`hb_unit()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_unit.md) | Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson | ✓ BYM2/Besag |
| **Two-Fold HB** | [`hb_twofold()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_twofold.md) | Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson | ✓ BYM2/Besag |

The Bayesian models are fitted with `engine = inla_engine()` (default).
[`hb_area()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_area.md),
[`hb_unit()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_unit.md)
and
[`hb_twofold()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_twofold.md)
can also be fitted by MCMC in Python (JAX/NumPyro) with
`engine = jax_engine()`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Performance at a Glance

#### 1. Frequentist EBLUP with analytical MSE (time and peak memory)

| Model ($`n = 1,000`$ domains, 5 covariates) | `fastsae` | `sae` | `emdi` |
|:---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **Fay-Herriot** | **0.000639 s** (1.91 MB) | 0.799 s (39.0 MB; 1,250x slower) | 13.5 s (222 MB; 21,071x slower) |
| **Spatial Fay-Herriot** | **0.518 s** (78.7 MB) | 24.1 s (239 MB; 46x slower) | 25.2 s (310 MB; 49x slower) |
| **Spatio-Temporal FH ($`T = 5`$), point estimates** | **39.8 s** (495 MB) | 1160 s (3.60 GB; 29x slower) | \- |

#### 2. Bayesian Beta models: INLA vs Stan MCMC (largest $`n`$ benchmarked)

| Model | $`n`$ | [`fastsae::hb_area`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_area.md) (INLA) | [`tipsae::fit_sae`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/tipsae/man/fit_sae.html) (Stan) | Ratio of times |
|:---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **Beta** | 1,000 | **3.73 s** | 180 s | 48x |
| **Spatial Beta (Besag ICAR)** | 1,000 | **4.28 s** | 362 s | 85x |
| **Spatio-Temporal Beta (Besag + RW1, $`T = 5`$)** | 50 | **3.80 s** | 716 s | 189x |

Times are medians of `bench::mark()`. The frequentist rows were measured
on 2026-10-26 with fastsae 1.0.0, sae 1.3 and emdi 2.2.3 on the same
simulated data sets (Apple M4, R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24);
`benchmarks/bench_frequentist.R`), each in its own R process; memory is
the increase of the peak resident memory of that process during the
fits, which includes memory allocated by compiled code (increases of a
few tens of MB vary from run to run and should not be compared). ‘sae’
has no analytical MSE for the spatio-temporal model, so that row
compares point estimates; with its analytical MSE, fastsae took 39.3 s.
The Bayesian `fastsae` rows were re-measured on 2026-10-14
(`benchmarks/bench_bayes_fastsae.R`), the `tipsae` rows (4 chains of
2,000 iterations) come from an earlier run on the same data. See the
[benchmark
article](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/benchmarks.html) for
all sizes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

``` r

# Install from CRAN (once published)
install.packages("fastsae")

# Or install the development version from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ridsonap/fastsae")
```

Explore detailed guides, worked examples, and performance analyses:

- [**Getting Started with
  fastsae**](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/getting-started.md):
  Step-by-step walkthrough of model fitting, diagnostics, and S3
  extraction.
- [**Spatial & Spatio-Temporal Models
  (EBLUP)**](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/spatial-temporal.md):
  Working with spatial weights matrices, spatial kriging, and
  spatio-temporal panels.
- [**Bayesian Area-Level Models
  (INLA)**](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/hb-area-inla.md):
  Hierarchical Bayesian SAE using INLA with 6 distributions and
  spatial-temporal effects.
- [**Model Diagnostics &
  Calibration**](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/model-diagnostics.md):
  Diagnostics and benchmarking to aggregate targets.
- [**Unit-Level Estimation
  (BHF)**](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/unit-level-bhf.md):
  Fitting the Battese-Harter-Fuller model with individual survey data.
- [**Performance
  Benchmarks**](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/benchmarks.md):
  Interactive charts and speedup comparisons across sample sizes.
- [**Function
  Reference**](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/index.md):
  Comprehensive API reference and parameter documentation.

## References

- Fay, R. E., & Herriot, R. A. (1979). Estimates of income for small
  places: An application of James-Stein procedures to Census data.
  *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 74(366), 269–277.
- Battese, G. E., Harter, R. M., & Fuller, W. A. (1988). An
  error-components model for prediction of county crop areas using
  survey and satellite data. *Journal of the American Statistical
  Association*, 83(401), 28–36.
- Marhuenda, Y., Molina, I., & Morales, D. (2013). Small area estimation
  with spatio-temporal Fay-Herriot models. *Computational Statistics &
  Data Analysis*, 58, 308–325.
- Pratesi, M., & Salvati, N. (2008). Small area estimation for spatially
  correlated data: A Fay-Herriot with the spatial linear spline model.
  *Journal of Applied Statistics*, 35(7), 781–794.
- Torabi, M., & Rao, J. N. K. (2014). On small area estimation under a
  semi-parametric mixed model. *Journal of Multivariate Analysis*, 124,
  226–236.
- Rue, H., Martino, S., & Chopin, N. (2009). Approximate Bayesian
  inference for latent Gaussian models using integrated nested Laplace
  approximations (with discussion). *Journal of the Royal Statistical
  Society: Series B*, 71(2), 319–392.
- Rao, J. N. K., & Molina, I. (2015). *Small Area Estimation* (2nd ed.).
  John Wiley & Sons.

# Package index

## Classical Area-Level Models (EBLUP)

High-performance C++ implementation of Fay-Herriot models

- [`eblup_fh()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_fh.md)
  : Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction based on a Fay-Herriot
  Model.
- [`eblup_sfh()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_sfh.md)
  : Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction based on a Spatial
  Fay-Herriot Model.
- [`eblup_stfh()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_stfh.md)
  : Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction based on a Spatio-Temporal
  Fay-Herriot Model.

## Bayesian Area-Level Models (INLA)

Hierarchical Bayesian SAE using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations
(INLA) across 6 distributions with spatial and spatio-temporal effects

- [`hb_area()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_area.md)
  : Hierarchical Bayes for Area-Level Small Area Estimation

## Estimation Engines

Engine objects for the Hierarchical Bayes models: INLA (default) or MCMC
with NumPyro / JAX (optional Python backend)

- [`inla_engine()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_engine.md)
  [`jax_engine()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_engine.md)
  [`print(`*`<fastsae_engine>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_engine.md)
  : Estimation engines for the Hierarchical Bayes models
- [`setup_numpyro_env()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/setup_numpyro_env.md)
  : Set up, or check, the Python environment for the NumPyro / JAX
  engine

## Two-Fold Subarea Models

Nested area-subarea level models (Torabi & Rao, 2014) with both area and
subarea random effects via REML EBLUP and Bayesian INLA

- [`eblup_twofold()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_twofold.md)
  : Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction under a Two-fold
  Fay-Herriot Model.
- [`hb_twofold()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_twofold.md)
  : Two-Fold Hierarchical Bayes for Sub-Area Level Small Area Estimation

## Unit-Level Models

Battese-Harter-Fuller models for unit-level survey data via REML EBLUP
and Bayesian INLA

- [`eblup_bhf()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/eblup_bhf.md)
  : Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (EBLUP) for the
  Battese-Harter-Fuller Model
- [`hb_unit()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/hb_unit.md)
  : Hierarchical Bayes for Unit-Level Small Area Estimation

## Pre-Modeling Utilities

Spatial weights, spatial autocorrelation tests, and smoothing of
sampling variances

- [`create_weights()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/create_weights.md)
  : Create Spatial Proximity and Weights Matrix
- [`spatial_test()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/spatial_test.md)
  : Pre-Modeling Spatial Diagnostic and Autocorrelation Tests
- [`gvf_smooth()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/gvf_smooth.md)
  : Generalized Variance Function (GVF) Smoothing for Sampling Variances

## Model Diagnostics & Visualization

Universal diagnostic framework and ggplot2 visualization methods

- [`diagnose()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/diagnose.md)
  : Diagnostic Evaluation of Small Area Estimation Models
- [`autoplot(`*`<fastsae_diagnose>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/autoplot.fastsae_diagnose.md)
  : Autoplot Method for fastsae_diagnose Objects

  : Summarize a fastsae object
- [`coef(`*`<fastsae>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/coef.fastsae.md)
  : Extract coefficients from a fastsae object

- [`residuals(`*`<fastsae>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/residuals.fastsae.md)
  : Extract residuals from a fastsae object

  : Print a fastsae object
- [`print(`*`<summary.fastsae>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/print.summary.fastsae.md)
  : Print summary of a fastsae object

## Benchmarking & Calibration

Calibrate small area estimates to aggregate targets via Ratio,
Difference, Optimal, and Logit methods (Rao & Molina, 2015)

- [`benchmark_sae()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/benchmark_sae.md)
  [`print(`*`<fastsae_benchmark>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/benchmark_sae.md)
  [`summary(`*`<fastsae_benchmark>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/benchmark_sae.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<fastsae_benchmark>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/benchmark_sae.md)
  [`plot(`*`<fastsae_benchmark>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/benchmark_sae.md)
  : Benchmark Small Area Estimation Predictions to Aggregate Targets

## Model Comparison & Spatial Mapping

Unified spatial choropleth mapping (‘satu pintu’), model concordance
evaluation, and official publication exports

- [`map_sae()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/map_sae.md)
  : Unified Spatial Choropleth Mapping for Small Area Estimates
- [`compare_sae()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/compare_sae.md)
  [`print(`*`<fastsae_comparison>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/compare_sae.md)
  [`summary(`*`<fastsae_comparison>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/compare_sae.md)
  [`plot(`*`<fastsae_comparison>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/compare_sae.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<fastsae_comparison>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/compare_sae.md)
  : Compare Two Small Area Estimation Models
- [`step_sae()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/step_sae.md)
  : Stepwise Selection of the Covariates of a Small Area Model
- [`export_sae()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/export_sae.md)
  : Export Small Area Estimation Results to Excel or CSV
- [`add_reliability_flags()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/add_reliability_flags.md)
  : Add Official Statistical Reliability Flags
- [`plot(`*`<fastsae>`*`)`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/plot.fastsae.md)
  : Plot method for fastsae objects

## Simulation & Synthetic Data Generation

Utilities to simulate area-level cross-sectional, panel, and spatial
weight matrices

- [`sim_area_data()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/sim_area_data.md)
  : Simulate Multi-Distribution Small Area Data with Spatial
  Autocorrelation
- [`sim_series_data()`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/sim_series_data.md)
  : Simulate Spatio-Temporal Multi-Distribution Small Area Data

## Example & Synthetic Datasets

Built-in empirical and synthetic survey datasets

- [`mys`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/mys.md) : mys:
  mean years of schooling of people with disabilities
- [`mys_panel`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/mys_panel.md)
  : mys_panel: mean years of schooling of people with disabilities,
  2016-2026
- [`mys_proxmat`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/mys_proxmat.md)
  : Example proximity matrix
- [`cornsoybean`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/cornsoybean.md)
  : Corn and Soybean Survey and Satellite Data in 12 Iowa Counties
- [`cornsoybeanmeans`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/cornsoybeanmeans.md)
  : Corn and Soybean Mean Number of Pixels per Segment for 12 Iowa
  Counties
- [`sim_area`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/sim_area.md)
  : Multi-Distribution Synthetic Area-Level Dataset
- [`sim_panel`](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/reference/sim_panel.md)
  : Multi-Distribution Spatio-Temporal Panel Dataset
